messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 49-year-old obese man presents to the emergency department with a fever and a cough productive of bloody sputum. He has also been waking up at night frequently, which he attributes to sweating while asleep. He is also proud of recently losing some weight but denies actively trying to do so. He says that he has had these symptoms intermittently for the last several years but has not consistently sought treatment because his housing has been transient with periods of homelessness. He is started on a course of therapy and leaves against medical advice before his physician is able to explain the medications. He returns two days later because he is concerned that his eyes are bleeding. The area of the lung most likely affected by this patient's condition has which of the following characteristics?

Options:
A. High perfusion, high ventilation, high V/Q ratio
B. High perfusion, high ventilation, low V/Q ratio
C. Low perfusion, high ventilation, high V/Q ratio
D. Low perfusion, low ventilation, high V/Q ratio
E. Low perfusion, low ventilation, low V/Q ratio

Correct answer: D. Low perfusion, low ventilation, high V/Q ratio

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This tests tuberculosis pathophysiology and V/Q relationships of the lung apices; psychiatric details (homelessness, leaving AMA) are incidental."}
